newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks ease in thin trade by break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks ease in thin trade by break.

text.p: Thai stocks declined slightly in thin trade by lunch break on Monday as investors sold shares in the absence of market moving news and on tight money market liquidity, brokers said.

"Liquidity is a bit tight because of heavy baht demand in the offshore market. Liquidity is expected to remain tight for the rest of this week because commercial banks have to meet reserve requirements later this week," said a broker at Securities One.
The SET index dropped 0.07 point to 566.32 on 920 million baht turnover by lunch.
All Thai commercial banks have to meet central bank reserve requirements on Friday.
Brokers said speculative buyers were active in the market this morning. Most stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of fresh, positive news to encourage them to enter the market.
Finance One, which resumed trading on Friday, topped the active list in terms of value, rising 0.20 baht to 7.20. Thai Farmers Bank lost one to 101 and Siam Cement shed two to 512.
